nodes.label: cratewise apply
nodes.rationale: --on-conflict overwrite moves the replaced file to ~/.music-cluster/backups/ so undo can restore it.

nodes.label: cratewise groups file
nodes.rationale: Overwriting is not offered because undo could not bring the replaced file back; run recorded as a 'Filing <group>' session so undo works.

nodes.label: cratewise undo
nodes.rationale: Refuses an operation a later session built on, so a replaced file is never lost; does not take back references added by --learn.

nodes.label: Overwrite backups for undo
nodes.rationale: The overwritten file is moved to ~/.music-cluster/backups/ rather than deleted; undo refuses if a later session filed to the same place so the replaced file is never lost.

nodes.rationale: Lets sorter, key and tempo changes be checked without the Mac; FMA cache (~16 GB) exceeds the 10 GB Actions limit.

nodes.label: Minor-loop key misread (relative major)
nodes.rationale: Averaged-chroma key match picks the relative major because its tonic occurs most often.

nodes.label: 4/3 tempo error fix (PR #35, SLOWER_CONSISTENCY_FLOOR)
nodes.rationale: A riff every three sixteenths gives the tracker a pulse a third faster than the kick; retrack at 3/4 tempo if bars hold together (consistency >= 0.66).

nodes.label: cratewise groups serato
nodes.rationale: Writes into Serato's own folder, so it previews and asks first, never replaces a crate it did not write, and tracks crates in _Serato_/cratewise-crates.json so --remove deletes exactly its own.

nodes.rationale: Tags already in files win; measured BPM/key/genre only fill gaps. Prefer playlist or copy for tracks a DJ app manages because moving breaks its link.

nodes.rationale: Every filing mode has a dry run first and an undo afterwards so no file changes without confirmation.

nodes.label: SPA layout (services/api.ts, stores, components, routes)
nodes.rationale: No server rendering: everything it reads exists only on the user's machine.

nodes.label: Background task polling (/api/tasks/{id})
nodes.rationale: Long-running analysis, sorting and discovery would otherwise hold a request open for minutes.

nodes.rationale: Applies the theme before first paint so the page never flashes the other theme.

nodes.label: cratewise prune
nodes.rationale: Never deletes audio files.

nodes.label: Auto-tagging (genre, beat type, mood, energy, danceability, key)
nodes.norm_label: auto-tagging (genre, beat type, mood, energy, danceability, key)
nodes.rationale: Every tag is a readable rule over measured quantities (music_cluster/tagging.py), not a trained model, so tags are explainable and wrong in explainable ways; tags never move a file or change a group.

nodes.label: Beat type measurement via averaged drum pattern
nodes.norm_label: beat type measurement via averaged drum pattern
nodes.rationale: Kick, snare and hat bands sampled twelve times per beat and folded into one bar; slow readings with busy sixteenths re-read at double time; swing from offbeat hat lateness.

nodes.label: beat_misses report table (PR #33)
nodes.rationale: Job logs are readable from the cloud while report artifacts on blob storage are not, so misses are printed in the summary.

nodes.label: Offbeat-grid four-to-the-floor fix (PR #34)
nodes.rationale: Techno misread as breakbeat when the beat grid sits half a beat off the kick; steady_kick counts against breakbeat.

nodes.label: Eval analysis cache (~/.music-cluster-eval/data/.cache)
nodes.rationale: Each file decoded once; re-analysed when measuring code (extractor.py, features.py, tagging.py, rhythm.py) changes.

nodes.label: AST pretrained embedding eval (--embedding ast)
nodes.rationale: Checks whether a network trained on lots of audio describes music better than the 96 hand features; not used in the app.

nodes.label: Auto-file operating points and threshold sweep
nodes.norm_label: auto-file operating points and threshold sweep

nodes.label: Baseline comparison with --tolerance
nodes.rationale: Exits non-zero if any headline number worsens by more than tolerance (default 0.02).

nodes.label: Calibration metrics (ece, brier, reliability)
nodes.rationale: Auto-filing trusts confidence, so 0.8 should mean right 80% of the time.

nodes.label: cratewise eval harness
nodes.rationale: Answers how well sorting, tagging and measuring work with numbers instead of a listening session.

nodes.label: Essentia optional reference
nodes.rationale: AGPL licence and non-commercial models keep it out of the app.

nodes.label: novelty_auroc metric
nodes.rationale: Does distance separate belongs-nowhere from belongs-somewhere tracks; 0.5 is chance.

nodes.label: Simulated libraries (sorting trials)
nodes.rationale: The sorter's job differs from a balanced genre benchmark, so each trial builds an imaginary library with 4-10 folders, a belongs-nowhere label, artist splits and 8-300 references.

nodes.label: Measuring/scoring changes judged by eval numbers
nodes.norm_label: measuring/scoring changes judged by eval numbers
nodes.rationale: Sorter or embedding changes need sorting-fma against datasets.json with tolerance 0.03; an unchanged synthetic run proves nothing about sorting.

nodes.label: Tags are readable rules, not trained models
nodes.norm_label: tags are readable rules, not trained models
nodes.rationale: Tags and sample categories are rules over measured quantities (tagging.py, samples.py, rhythm.py) so a user can see why a track got its tag.

nodes.label: Artist-based splits ground rule
nodes.rationale: Prevents artist leakage between references and queries.

nodes.label: librosa + FFmpeg decoding
nodes.rationale: Any format FFmpeg can decode is supported; features extracted from decoded PCM so format barely affects sorting.

nodes.label: Upgrading from 1.x (clustering-era migration)
nodes.rationale: Old clusterings were anonymous groupings; the new workflow is built on named groups, so only features are kept.

nodes.label: Frozen API Tauri sidecar
nodes.rationale: The packaged app must work for someone who never installed Python, so the API is frozen into one binary started by the shell on a free port.

nodes.label: Pinned ruff 0.15.8
nodes.rationale: A new ruff release can reformat code an older one left alone.

nodes.norm_label: app screens (overview, groups, sort, discover, library, settings)

nodes.label: Group crate colour
nodes.rationale: Marks the group on the Groups screen, pickers, score bars and queue so crates are told apart at a glance.

nodes.label: Centroid plus k-nearest-reference distance
nodes.rationale: Centroid is stable for small groups, kNN handles folders with several sounds; per-group scale normalization is off by default because it dropped recall on small crates (10% vs 32%).

nodes.label: Unmatched (matches nothing) via novelty
nodes.rationale: A track too far from every group is reported as matching nothing rather than forced into the least-bad group.

nodes.rationale: Large dependencies or models need Jules's approval; PyInstaller may miss imports, only build.yml catches that.

nodes.norm_label: dry run and undo for every filing mode
nodes.rationale: Every organizer.py filing mode ships with a dry run and an undo so file moves are reversible.

nodes.rationale: PEP 585/604 ruff rules are ignored on purpose; annotate only new code.

nodes.label: Never touch user files without confirmation
nodes.norm_label: never touch user files without confirmation
nodes.rationale: The tool scores, the user confirms, then it files; it never invents a category or touches an unconfirmed file.

nodes.norm_label: testing layers (unit, closed loop, ui unit, browser, screenshots)

nodes.norm_label: files stay put until you say so (dry run, undo, four filing modes)

nodes.rationale: For looking at the UI, mainly for agents; not a regression suite.

nodes.label: CLI conventions (--collection, --profile, --workers, recursion)
nodes.rationale: Nothing is written without asking: analysing, sorting, reviewing and discovering only change the database; audio files are touched only by apply (after preview and confirmation) and undo.

nodes.label: cratewise samples classify
nodes.rationale: Read-only check that the tool hears samples the way the user does before building a collection.

nodes.label: Collection profile (music vs sample)
nodes.rationale: Fixed at creation because stored features, fitted space and group references all assume one kind of audio; sorting both needs two collections sharing one database.

nodes.label: Discovery workflow for an unsorted pile
nodes.norm_label: discovery workflow for an unsorted pile
nodes.rationale: Candidate piles are only suggestions; nothing becomes a group until the user promotes it.

nodes.label: LDA blended with PCA feature space
nodes.norm_label: lda blended with pca feature space
nodes.rationale: LDA finds directions separating the user's groups; PCA components keep general audio structure so a track resembling nothing owned can still be noticed.

nodes.label: Sample profile analysis (one-shot measurements)
nodes.rationale: A one-shot's attack is its most identifying feature, so analysis starts at the first sample, never excerpts, and steps four times more finely; 29 extra event measurements (ADSR, eight bands, pitch) separate clap from snare.

nodes.label: Sample candidate naming from filename and audio
nodes.norm_label: sample candidate naming from filename and audio
nodes.rationale: Filenames in sample libraries are usually the truth; audio covers packs named Sample 04.wav.

nodes.label: Two promises (you define the groups; nothing on disk changes until you say so)
nodes.norm_label: two promises (you define the groups; nothing on disk changes until you say so)
nodes.rationale: Shapes the whole workflow: groups come from folders or explicitly kept candidates; audio files are only touched on commit after a preview, and every commit can be undone.

nodes.label: No invented tempo for single hits
nodes.norm_label: no invented tempo for single hits
nodes.rationale: Beat tracking a 400 ms kick returns a meaningless number, so a single hit records no BPM.

nodes.label: User-defined groups principle
nodes.rationale: The tool never invents a category and never moves a file the user has not confirmed; the user's folders are the training data.
